hints.content: The arrow points to all values less than $-2$.
And the point at $-2$ is *not* filled in.
So, the inequality represents everything strictly **less than $-2$.**

question.content:
**Choose the inequality that represents the following graph.**



[[☃ image 1]]

[[☃ radio 1]]

options.alt: A number line from negative 5 to 5 with evenly spaced tick marks in increments of 1. A line going to the left starts at negative 2 and continues left. An open point is plotted at negative 2 where the line begins.

choices.clue:
The graph of $x \leq -2$ actually looks like this:

![A number line from negative 5 to 5 with evenly spaced tick marks in increments of 1. A closed point is plotted at negative 2. A line running to the left starts at negative 2 and continues.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/0eff3734aef680fee7a88cdc7cd62916ae27a817)

The graph of $x > -2$ actually looks like this:

![A number line from negative 5 to 5 with evenly spaced tick marks in increments of 1. A line going to the right starts at negative 2 and continues right. An open point is plotted at negative 2 where the line begins.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/afa432e0fc66c7be733566b3be9f88734fd4937c)

The graph of $x \geq -2$ actually looks like this:

![A number line from negative 5 to 5 with evenly spaced tick marks in increments of 1. A line going to the right starts at negative 2 and continues right. A closed point is plotted at negative 2 where the line begins.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/7311a74a7c3748f08bbc4bbf6d772775a59e933b)
